title: Rice Pudding
subtitle: Slow-baked British rice pudding with nutmeg and cream
excerpt: Short-grain rice slow-baked in sweetened milk and cream until thick, silky, and deeply comforting. A golden skin forms on top; the rice underneath is tender and yielding.
sourceNotes: Rice pudding has been made in Britain since the Tudor period. The baked version with a nutmeg skin became the standard British nursery pudding and remains one of the most enduring comfort foods in the British kitchen.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Leftovers keep in the fridge for two days. Reheat gently with a splash of milk.

content.text: A low oven and a long bake are non-negotiable; higher heat produces a skin too quickly and leaves the rice undercooked beneath.

items.prepNote: or any short-grain pudding rice; rinsed

content.text: Tip the rice into a shallow baking dish, about 1.5 litres capacity.
Combine the milk, cream, and honey in a jug. Stir until the honey dissolves.
Pour the liquid over the rice. Stir once to combine.
Dot the butter over the surface. Scatter over the nutmeg.
Bake for 30 minutes. Stir once to prevent the rice from settling in one layer.
Bake for a further 1 hour 30 minutes without stirring until a golden skin has formed and the pudding is thick and creamy beneath.

items.symptom: Rice is still chalky after 2 hours.
items.cause: Oven ran too cool or dish was very deep.
items.fix: Stir, cover with foil, and bake for 30 more minutes.

items.cause: Milk ratio was high for the dish size.
items.fix: Return uncovered to the oven for 20 to 30 minutes to reduce.
Cover loosely with foil for the rest of the cooking time.
